title: Quotient and remainder of a successor
statement: Let $n>0$ and $i$ be natural numbers. If the remainder of $i$ upon division by $n$, increased by one, equals $n$, then the quotient of $i+1$ upon division by $n$ is the quotient of $i$ plus one, and the new remainder is zero. If the remainder of $i$ increased by one is not $n$, then the quotient is unchanged and the new remainder is the previous remainder plus one.
hypotheses_covered: $i\bmod n+1\ne n$ in the second implication
